verdict.text: All six round 1 findings are fixed.
The relabel left one stale number behind: the Conclusion still says "eight false alarms" where the Results now say seven (f7).
It is a one-word fix that does not need another look.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration and eval rows r1, r2 and r3 all pass.
Output: "stamp green: cdfa89cdf90d4d9c1b8d7a417065977afd549dd474b92ba29bf48936d957affb", the fingerprint this round is bound to.
r3 now runs `okf_validate.py .okf --strict` too.
Ran score.py: it prints 32 claims (10 gap, 7 false alarm, 15 recorded in the unit), precision 10/17 (59%, Wilson 36% to 78%), and the five other readings (9/16, 25/32, 10/32, 9/17, 8/17).
These match the README table line for line, and the verdict is still build.
The `same_change` reading uses labels.json's new `same_change` list of the two MIT units.
labels.json: 3b1acae3 is now `gap`, with a note saying it was relabelled after review.
Ran leak_check.py: AUC 0.64 for words and 0.50 for paths, and it prints the per-word rates.
"entry", "bundle" and "summary" lead, as the README says.
The usage line names leak_check.py itself.
The signals.py and judge.py docstrings now say every path under .okf/ and .loop/ is dropped for every unit, which matches hide.visible_files.
README description, prototypes index line and log line all say 32 claims, 15 recorded in the unit, and 10 of the other 17 gaps.
Did not run judge.py.
f1 resolved: the description, the index and the log now give 32 claims first, then 15 recorded in the unit and 10 of 17.
f2 resolved: the README defines precision, says the recorded-in-unit category was added after the run, and has a table of the other readings from score.py with the thin-margin caveat.
The Conclusion repeats the interval and the two-flip point.

f4 resolved: both docstrings describe hiding .okf/ and .loop/ for every unit.
f5 resolved: leak_check.py prints the per-word breakdown the README cites.
f6 resolved: r3 runs the strict validator, and the stamp shows it passing.

Change it to seven.
